sources.title: #data-insights: invoice API traffic mix
sources.author: P37
sources.text: Ran the numbers on invoice API traffic since the bulk import launch in January. Writes are now 58% of requests, up from 31% last year. It is not read-heavy any more, so caching reads will not move p95 much. Full breakdown in the notebook; happy to walk anyone through it.

sources.title: Churn exit survey, Q3 summary
sources.author: P23
sources.text: Exit survey, 212 responses from accounts that churned between June and August. Price is the top reason for only 14% of them. Missing integrations (41%) and setup friction (27%) rank well above it. Recommendation: stop treating churn as a pricing problem.

sources.title: Where merge time actually goes
sources.author: P05
sources.text: Measured 1,140 merged pull requests since March. Flaky test reruns account for 9% of time-to-merge. Waiting for a first review accounts for 61%. The merge queue helped because it batches merges, not because it fixed flakiness.

sources.title: #data-insights: what the cloud bill is made of
sources.author: P38
sources.text: Broke down June's bill by service. Analytics is 11% of it. Storage for invoice PDFs is 38% and egress is 22%. Moving analytics will not bend the curve.

sources.title: Latency profile of the invoice API
sources.author: P03
sources.text: Profiled the invoice API for a week. Synchronous PDF rendering is 61% of p95 latency; database time is 18%.

sources.title: #payments: delivery failure breakdown
sources.author: P13
sources.text: Of last month's failed invoice deliveries, 83% are bounces on the provider side, mostly throttling.

sources.title: Why invoices get paid late: 30 customer calls
sources.author: P15
sources.text: Thirty calls with finance teams. Twenty-two said paying by bank transfer is the slow part; only four said they forget.

sources.title: Decision record D-101: Cache invoice reads in Redis
sources.author: P01
sources.text:
Context: p95 latency on the invoice list has crept up to over 400 ms and is the top complaint from large accounts.
Decision: Cache invoice reads in Redis.
Why: Invoice API traffic is read-heavy, so caching reads cuts latency.
Options considered and not chosen: Add read replicas; Paginate the invoice list more aggressively.
Risks: cache invalidation bugs could show stale invoice totals.
Success means api p95 latency changes by -30.0% from its pre-launch level by 2026-04-20. Owner of the result: Aarav Sharma.
Discussed in SRC-0008.

sources.text:

sources.title: Decision record D-105: Switch email delivery provider
sources.author: P12
sources.text:

sources.author: P22
sources.text:
Maya: Proposal: retire the annual plan discount. The exit survey says price is not why customers leave.
Theo: Did we consider the other option, 'Keep the discount for existing annual customers'?
Elif: Fine by me as long as we can turn it off quickly.
Ivan: Worried about annual signups dip. Can we roll it out to a few accounts first?
Jonas: Going ahead. Decision record to follow.

sources.title: Decision record D-126: Retire the annual plan discount
sources.author: P21
sources.text:
Context: The exit survey says price is not why customers leave.
Decision: Retire the annual plan discount.
Why: not written down.
Options considered and not chosen: Keep the discount for existing annual customers.
Risks: annual signups dip.
No success metric was set.
Discussed in SRC-0058.

sources.title: #payments: batch small invoices into weekly statements
sources.author: P13
sources.text:
Karan: Proposal: batch small invoices into weekly statements. Customers with many small invoices write in asking for one statement.
Tara: Can we write down what success looks like before we start?
Nikhil: Fine by me as long as we can turn it off quickly.
Nikhil: Agree. Let's not over-design it.
Nikhil: Happy to pair on this, I touched that code last month.
Neha: Going ahead. Decision record to follow.

sources.title: Decision record D-127: Batch small invoices into weekly statements
sources.author: P12
sources.text:
Context: Customers with many small invoices write in asking for one statement.
Decision: Batch small invoices into weekly statements.
Why: Customers are annoyed by receiving many small invoices.
Options considered and not chosen: Let customers choose per client.
Risks: statements confuse accounting exports.
Success means support tickets per week changes by -10.0% from its pre-launch level by 2026-09-21. Owner of the result: Neha Moreau.
Discussed in SRC-0060.

sources.title: #growth: translate the app into german
sources.author: P23
sources.text:
Felix: Proposal: translate the app into german. German prospects make up most of the EU pipeline.
Sara: Fine by me as long as we can turn it off quickly.
Maya: Worried about support in German. Can we roll it out to a few accounts first?
Nora: Agree. Let's not over-design it.
Nora: Happy to pair on this, I touched that code last month.
Jonas: Going ahead. Decision record to follow.

sources.title: Decision record D-128: Translate the app into German
sources.author: P21
sources.text:
Context: German prospects make up most of the EU pipeline.
Decision: Translate the app into German.
Why: EU prospects stall because the product is only in English.
Options considered and not chosen: Hire a German-speaking salesperson first.
Risks: support in German.
Success means eu signups per week changes by +50.0% from its pre-launch level by 2026-06-08. Owner of the result: Jonas Kapoor.
Discussed in SRC-0062.

sources.title: #data: move analytics to a columnar warehouse
sources.author: P37
sources.text:
Arun: Proposal: move analytics to a columnar warehouse. The infrastructure bill grew 12% in March.
Pooja: How sure are we this moves infrastructure cost per month? Do we have numbers, or is this a hunch?
Hana: Is this the most important thing for this quarter?
Chloe: Going ahead. Decision record to follow.

sources.title: Decision record D-129: Move analytics to a columnar warehouse
sources.author: P36
sources.text:
Context: The infrastructure bill grew 12% in March.
Decision: Move analytics to a columnar warehouse.
Why: Analytics queries drive most of the infrastructure bill.
Options considered and not chosen: Reserved instances; Archive old invoice PDFs.
Risks: analysts must learn a new tool.
Success means infrastructure cost per month changes by -15.0% from its pre-launch level by 2026-07-27. Owner of the result: Chloe Weber.
Discussed in SRC-0064.

sources.title: #platform: create a second on-call rotation
sources.author: P03
sources.text:
Rohan: Proposal: create a second on-call rotation. Platform engineers were paged 41 times in August.
Kabir: +1, this has bitten us twice this quarter.
Ananya: We looked at 'Hire an SRE first' last quarter. Slower to ship, and it does not fix the root cause.
Aarav: Going ahead. Decision record to follow.

sources.title: Decision record D-130: Create a second on-call rotation
sources.author: P01
sources.text:
Context: Platform engineers were paged 41 times in August.
Decision: Create a second on-call rotation.
Why: not written down.
Options considered and not chosen: Hire an SRE first.
Risks: thin rotations burn people out faster.
No success metric was set.
Discussed in SRC-0066.
